All 40 lowerBound values AND all 40 numberOfCharacters counts are byte-identical to stored at the stored 1 dp precision, so upstream is genuinely frozen and not merely stamped frozen. Nothing merged; the coverage date correctly does not move. This is the OWNER-ACCEPTED standing red on this requirement — it clears when WoWMeta re-runs its pipeline, and must not be acked away or absorbed by raising maxAgeDays.

Fetched cleanly, and upstream has NOT recut since the stored snapshot — which is why this is partial rather than success. All three meta pages fetched by plain browser-UA GET (r.jina.ai does not work on murlok), HTTP 200. The page's own <time datetime="2026-08-25T02:45:24Z"> is the data's real date; the neighbouring "Updated 13 seconds ago" prose is a server-rendered relative string and must NOT be read as freshness — taking it at face value would have produced a success row on 19-hour-old data, the exact shape the wowmeta pinned-manifest lesson warns about. Parse reconciliation matters here and caught a real defect: a first pass split on the full opening anchor and returned 24 DPS / 6 healer / 4 tank = 34 rows, which would have merged a SHORT roster while looking healthy; splitting on the bare meta-item token gives 27 + 7 + 6 = 40, 0 unmatched, 0 duplicates, reconciled against the roster shape before anything was written. Every one of the 40 'Top-50 avg M+ rating (ceiling)' values is identical to stored, consistent with the page's unchanged timestamp, so nothing was merged. The name keeps its '(ceiling)' qualifier deliberately — this is the average rating of each spec's own top-50 players, not popularity and not a population mean, and must never be read as either.

All 27 DPS charts requested via talent_target_scaling/castingpatchwerk, up to 3 attempts each, then the failures re-probed 5 more times apiece alongside a control spec. 18 returned data; 9 returned the ambiguous 76-byte {"status": "error", "message": "No standard chart with these values found."} body on 8 of 8 attempts each — Havoc, Balance, Feral, Augmentation, Devastation, Retribution, Elemental Shaman, Arms, Fury — while the control (Subtlety Rogue) succeeded 5 of 5 interleaved in the same minutes, so the endpoint is demonstrably healthy and those specs simply are not published right now. The upstream set MOVED since last night, which is worth recording: Devourer and Windwalker have appeared (17 -> 18 available) while Elemental Shaman has dropped out, and every one of the 18 charts is re-timestamped 2026-08-26 against last night's 2026-08-19/2026-08-24 — bloodmallet is actively re-simming. NOTHING WAS MERGED, which remains the only correct outcome for three independent reasons: every chart carries simc_settings.tier MID2 (read off the payload, never assumed; simc_settings.ptr is the STRING "0" and was compared explicitly) against MID1 in all 26 stored profiles, and a source's fight-profile pool may hold exactly one tier — fightLabels pools every DPS profile with no provenance key and MID2 measured a mean 1.79x MID1, so a mixed pool would publish which specs have been re-simmed as if it were spec strength; 18 of the 26 stored specs is below the 19-row drop floor; and Augmentation is absent by design, so even a 'complete' MID2 roster will be 26. fightProfile.asOf stays each spec's own chart date (2026-07-08 for 25 specs, 2026-07-15 for Elemental), the age gate stays red, and that red is the honest signal that upstream has not finished re-simming. Adopt wholesale on the first run where all 26 publish MID2.

MID1_Raid.txt is 272 bytes — a run that has just STARTED, no "DPS Ranking:" block — and its header reads 12.1.0.69497 Live (hotfix 2026-08-26/69497, git build HEAD 0711f60438), so MID1 is being re-simmed on TODAY's live build. MID1_Raid.html is still the completed 12.0.7.68974 Live report (hotfix 2026-08-06/68974, git build 678e66d384) — the same git hash last night's run recorded, which is the honest explanation for an unchanged parse rather than a fresh sim, and it matches the stored asOf 2026-08-08 exactly, so there is nothing newer to parse for the stored series. MID2_Raid.txt is now a completed run on the same 12.1.0.69497 Live build (last night it was 12.1.0.69465) and DOES carry a DPS Ranking block, but the roster is still PARTIAL: 36 profiles resolving by longest-prefix (hyphen allowed) to 18 of 27 roster DPS specs, missing Havoc, Devourer, Balance, Feral, Devastation, Retribution, Arms and Fury plus Augmentation which is absent by design. Adopting it would both mix two sim tiers in one rank pool and drop the stored series 26 -> 18, a 31% row drop past the 25% limit. Nothing merged; stored values byte-identical at 2026-08-08. OWNER-ACCEPTED standing red — it clears when a complete Live MID2 report lands, which continues to look close now that both reports simulate on the same live build. Era-verified off the header build string, not the visible "12.3.0", which is the Highcharts version.

Fetched and parsed cleanly, and DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED: upstream has rolled to a new weekly period that has barely started. /period/latest now 302s to /period/1078 (HTTP 200, 328,504 bytes) where the stored rows came from 1077; the body names it "Period 1078, week 2 of MID2" and carries the site's own red banner "This period just started and is still in progress", with "Top 2000 keys, 10000 characters (7671 unique), 10.6 average key level" against 1077's completed 2895 unique at 15.3 average key level — i.e. a day-one, low-key sample, not a comparable week. Parse bounded to the "Spec representation in top keys" section (scanning the whole page yields far more rows because the classes block and per-dungeon sections repeat the pattern), labels normalised across the lowercase-hyphenated form ("devourer demon-hunter"), value taken from the <span class="mt-1"> AFTER the bar's height style, never the height itself: 40 rows, 0 unmatched — Fire Mage is present this period, where it was absent from 1077's chart entirely. Shape checks pass, confirming this is the representation SHARE column and not the /meta per-key-presence figure: sum 100.10% with role subtotals DPS 60.1 / Tank 20.0 / Healer 20.0, matching the page's own group headings (Ranged 35.3%, Melee 24.7%, Tank 20%, Healer 20.1%). The reason for holding is measured, not cautious: 33 of 40 values move, many far past maxValueMovePct 0.6 — Restoration Druid 0.1 -> 1.4, Beast Mastery 0.6 -> 4.8, Frost Mage 0.1 -> 0.5, Blood DK 13 -> 7.4, Arms 12.7 -> 6.1 — so merging would trip the value-move gate, and that gate has NO agent-writable proposal channel by design. Stored 1077 rows are byte-identical and their coverage date correctly does not move. Fix path for a human: either re-run the workflow with value_move_ack once period 1078 has matured into a comparable week, or simply let a later run merge it when the week is complete — the latter is preferred, since a day-one sample is not the quantity this series publishes.

THREE discovery channels swept, not one. (1) Wowhead news RSS: HTTP 200, 179,289 bytes, 40 items parsed per <item> block (never by tag adjacency), newest 2026-08-25T20:34 -05:00. (2) The news INDEX, because it leads the RSS within a run — data.news.newsData extracted by anchoring on the id attribute and brace-balancing from there (string-aware), 20 posts, top id 382626, identical head to the RSS so nothing landed mid-run. (3) The Wowhead blue-tracker index (data.blueTracker.default, 50 entries deduped by topic), which is the channel that actually carried tonight's find. ONE NEW FEED ENTRY LOGGED: the August 25 live hotfix round-up, kind "hotfix", read from the canonical source rather than a mirror — Kaivax's rolling hotfix blue post, us.forums topic 2336376, whose title has rolled to "World of Warcraft: Midnight Hotfixes - August 25" and whose post 1 was edited 2026-08-25T17:11:23Z to append that section (72,987 chars, read with its <ul> nesting INTACT). Exactly ONE class line in it is new to this feed — Unholy Death Knight, "Resolved an issue causing the Unholy Devotion attack speed increase to also reduce attack damage and therefore have a neutral effect" — and it classifies NULL under classifyHighlight (checked, not assumed) because its clauses mix an increase with a reduce, so it does not vote in the outlook tally. The other 14 class lines are the already-logged 2026-08-22 tuning pass restated verbatim as it shipped; they were compared line by line and match at identical values, and were deliberately NOT re-distilled because the tally counts LINES and logging them twice would double-count one pass — the same reasoning that excludes the launch patch notes. That check also settles the tier-set question: both set-bonus lines (Restoration Druid 4-piece Genesis +8s, Retribution Paladin 4-piece Divine Arbiter +150%/+75%) are unchanged from the announcing post, whose date their spec.tierSet entries already carry, so no tierSet needed advancing and the upkeep gate is quiet honestly. The post's large PLAYER VERSUS PLAYER section (20+ specs) is out of scope for this PvE tracker and was not distilled.
